EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Cancellations improved across every headline metric in Week 29: value down 24.9% to R1.43M, quantity down 25.8% to 9,947 units, and the official rate improved 0.38pp to 4.84%. Stock Integrity - Dispo & stock management is the leading driver by value this week (43 of 106 investigated lines, R111,443.06), ahead of Open Boxes and Product Sold Out. Apple 13" MacBook Air M4 Chip, Black was the single highest-value cancelled SKU (R83,473.02).
◎
KEY TAKEAWAY
The improvement is real across value, quantity, and rate -- but stock-integrity and process-adherence issues (Dispo, Open Boxes) remain the largest single driver by value, not customer-side cancellations. Woodmead remains the highest-value store (R220,247.58) despite the week-on-week improvement, and the Top 10 stores account for 66.1% of all cancelled value.

5 KEY FINDINGS
  • Cancellation rate improved from 5.22% to 4.84% (-0.38pp) week-on-week.
  • Value reduced 24.9% and quantity reduced 25.8% week-on-week.
  • Stock Integrity - Dispo & stock management is the #1 driver by value this week (43 of 106 investigated lines, R111,443.06) -- a stock-integrity/process issue, not a customer-side cancellation.
  • Open Boxes - Non-adherence to S20 Process is #2 by value (13 lines, R93,548.70) -- also a process-adherence issue, not demand-driven.
  • By quantity, Shelf Replenishment is the largest driver (88 of 174 investigated lines) -- a different leading cause than by value, meaning value and volume are being driven by different root causes this week.
  • Apple 13" MacBook Air M4 Chip, Black is the highest-value cancelled SKU this week (R83,473.02, 6 units).
  • Woodmead remains the highest-value store for cancellations (R220,247.58) despite the week's overall improvement.

evidence_status.note: This is a hand-built custom_html one-pager (house-style approximation, not a new schema section type -- see AGENTS.md/CLAUDE_CODEX_WORKING_PROTOCOL.md scope decision). All figures were independently computed from Cancellations_10_Jul_-_16_July_2026.xlsx (Export, Top 10 Stores, Top 15 Product, Division sheets) and Cheryl_Cancellation_Feedback_10_July_2026.xlsx (Value/Qty investigation sheets), and reconcile exactly to the WOW sheet's official Week 29 totals (R1,434,333.02 / 9,947 units / 4.84% / 3.98%). The 'Auto-cancel (no picker)' KPI is a DERIVED proxy (blank Picker field on cancelled lines: R288,930.98, 20.14% of value) -- it does not have a single authoritative source column and should be read as directional, not official. Week 28 daily figures were not available in the supplied data and are honestly omitted from the daily chart rather than estimated. A prior AI-generated HTML analysis file (cancellations_wk28_29_analysis.html) was reviewed but its daily breakdown did not reconcile to the true weekly total (summed to R1,644,418 against a true R1,434,333) and was not used; its per-reason value breakdown did independently reconcile and matches this report's figures.

provenance.extraction_notes: All headline KPIs, daily breakdown, top stores, top products, division split, and reason investigation tallies were independently computed from the raw source files, not transcribed from any prior report or screenshot. Total value (R1,434,333.02), quantity (9,947), and both cancellation rates were cross-verified against the WOW sheet's own pre-computed Week 29 row and match exactly. Division and Top-10-Stores totals independently sum to the same total value. A reference style image (prior Makro CSAT/Cancellations one-pager) was used for visual layout only -- one of its own data points (MacBook Air M4 cancellation value) did not reconcile against the fresh raw exports supplied for this report (image implied R33,473.02; the raw pivot data, internally consistent with its own per-store breakdown, gives R83,473.02), confirming the image was not used as a data source.
